newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World to expand China retail business.
newsitem.headline: New World to expand China retail business.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd plans to invest up to HK$1 billion in expanding its chain of department stores in China, managing director Henry Cheng said on Thursday at a news conference.
"We have invested over HK$100 million in the business so far and we expect our investment in the business will be within HK$1 billion," Cheng said.
Cheng said existing department stores were expected to bring in profits in the next two to three years, which would be reinvested into the business later on.
New World has three department stores to date in China. Its store in Wuhan, Hubei province, opened in 1994, while the one in Shenyang, Liaoning province started in December 1995.
The store in Wuxi, Jiangsu province began in June 1996.
Earnings prospects were positive, Cheng said, citing the company's Wuhan store which had an earnings growth of over 50 percent in its second year of operation.
Cheng said stores would be opened in Tianjin and Beijing by mid-1997, and Harbin, in Heilongjiang province by end-1996.
Stores in Qingdao in Shandong province, Nanjing in Jiangsu province, Dalian in Liaoning province and Ningbo in Zhejiang province, would be opened over the next two years, he said.
